title: Review: list_orders performance smell

findings.summary: list_orders already loads tenant rows via list_by_tenant, then calls get_order per row (extra cache/DB fetches per order).

title: Review: cache vs status change (I4)

findings.summary: mark_paid updates order status to paid but never calls cache.invalidate_order (unlike cancel_order), so a prior get_order cache entry can keep serving the old status after payment.

title: Incident: duplicate OrderPaid

title: Constrained fix: webhook idempotency

plan_steps: or use transactional outbox with unique webhook_id

raw_content:
I'll inspect the shopapi webhook and order-payment flow so the fix is grounded in real code, not vibes.The README already screams I3 — reading the webhook path and outbox next.Lo and behold — some earlier developer ordered the gates like a drunk nightwatchman. `handle_payment_webhook` checks `processed_webhooks`, then cheerfully `outbox.insert(order_paid(...))`, and only *after* that calls `_mark_processed`. Provider retries (see `worker/webhook_retry.py`) sail through and double-insert `OrderPaid`. “What’s done cannot be undone” — unless you undo the ordering, you fools.

Minimal fix: one file, move the idempotency record *before* the outbox write. Keep the HTTP entrypoint; no new broker.
